object.title: Knight Capital 2012: Evidence-Bounded Retrolongitudinal Reconstruction
object.summary: Author and corresponding creator (Knight case draft): Juan Antonio Marín Liera · ORCID https://orcid.org/0009-0002-3714-1467 · System Friction Institute. Research-method and real historical documentary case for the August 1, 2012 Knight Capital technology failure. Official SEC/EDGAR source vintages support a retrospective sequence from reported financial outcome to server deployment, warning signals, incident response and documented dependencies. MIHM-T historical and retrolongitudinal study eligibility are accepted. LCI agent individuation and frozen SFI-DT confirmatory prediction are not established. A publication candidate is not a validated predictive model.

findings.title: Official reports of a real trading disruption
findings.summary: Knight Capital publicly reported approximately US$440 million in pretax realized losses on August 2, 2012. A later October 2013 SEC order reported losses exceeding US$460 million. These are different publication vintages, not a single timeless measurement.

findings.title: Later regulator-documented technical and response sequence
findings.summary: SEC Exchange Act Release 34-70694 (October 16, 2013) describes inconsistent SMARS server deployment, 97 premarket internal warning emails, erroneous execution activity and an incident intervention involving removal of updated code that aggravated the problem. These statements summarize retrospective SEC findings, not details publicly known on August 1, 2012.

findings.title: Reconstruction admissibility is not predictive validation
findings.summary: A dated source-view selector and retrolongitudinal reconstruction on the official case are reproducible software methods. Original operator intent, actual sign-off, precise rollback timing and independently measured counterfactual outcome are unknown. No blind MIHM-T prediction, LCI individuation metric or frozen DT structural fidelity is established.

limitations: The official SEC regulatory order was issued in 2013 and does not establish publicly available Knight-specific 2012 pre-incident knowledge.
Regulatory findings are retrospective documentary claims; no original SMARS logs or human authorization receipts are held in this research package.
The study is neither a blind forecast nor a causal counterfactual identification, and its methods are not scientifically validated.
Authorship of any additional contributors and publication-specific licensing require review; the Institute's source repository is proprietary.
